trigger: a delegated fork audit claimed 32/32 (later corrected to 121/121) MCP tools fail the A5 'typed output schema' criterion, citing kObjectOutputSchema as a generic placeholder used everywhere
provenance: parsed kTools[] directly with a script (not delegated): 121/121 tools have real, distinct, properly-typed output_schema_json fields at the DISCOVERY layer (what tools/list advertises) -- zero use the generic placeholder, zero omit it. kObjectOutputSchema is a SEPARATE, unrelated mechanism used at 113 individual tool_result() call sites purely as a non-null sentinel deciding whether structuredContent is populated in a given RESPONSE -- its value is never rendered (tool_result's own body only checks output_schema_json for null-ness). The fork conflated these two mechanisms. Verified by reading tool_result()'s implementation directly.
summary: A delegated audit's central finding (output-schema gap on all MCP tools) was FALSE -- verified by direct parsing before any fix work was scoped around it, preventing a wasted multi-tool schema-rewrite effort

trigger: 5 Guardian MCP tools' degraded-query branch (guardian_status_rollup/list_rules/guardian_rule_agent_status_rows/guardian_device_all_guards returning nullopt) used bare error_response() with no data field, while GET /guaranteed-state/status's identical condition explicitly carries retry_after_ms=5000 (rest_api_v1.cpp, with a comment distinguishing it from the non-transient unwired-gate/null-store 503s)
provenance: read every flagged handler's full body directly (not regex-only) to confirm each occurrence was the genuine query-fault branch, not the correctly-non-retryable store-pointer-null misconfiguration guard that precedes it in the same handler; verified REST's own retry_after_ms=5000 value at rest_api_v1.cpp before applying the identical value to MCP
summary: 5 Guardian MCP tools (get_guardian_status, list_guardian_rules, get_guardian_rule_status x2 branches, get_guardian_device_guards) now carry retry_after_ms=5000 on their degraded-store branch, matching the REST twin

trigger: list_workflows/get_workflow/get_workflow_execution/list_schedules' MCP query-fault branches (genericize_db_error-wrapped) omitted retry_after_ms while their REST v1 twins (workflow_routes.cpp) explicitly pass {.retry_after_ms=5000} on the identical condition
provenance: cross-checked each MCP call site against its REST twin's exact source line before fixing (not assumed); list_schedules was found as a 4th instance beyond the original 3-tool scope during this same read-through, same PR (#4030) same bug class
summary: 4 Workflows/Schedules MCP tools now carry retry_after_ms=5000 on their query-fault branch, matching their REST twins exactly (value cross-checked per site, not assumed uniform)

trigger: export_definition + the pre-existing (non-Batch-A) get_definition tool's query-fault branch omitted retry_after_ms while GET /api/v1/instructions/{id}/export ALSO omitted it (a symmetric gap, both sides fixed to 5000); list_product_packs/get_product_pack's query-fault branch omitted a CONDITIONAL retry hint -- product_pack_error_status() classifies the underlying error as 503 (genuine DB/lease fault, transient) vs 400 (validation/business-rule error, never retryable), and neither REST nor MCP applied that classification to the retry hint before this fix
provenance: read product_pack_error_status()'s full implementation (product_pack_model.cpp:53) before fixing to confirm the 503-vs-400 classification exists and is authoritative; applied retry_after_ms=5000 CONDITIONALLY on res.status==503 (REST) / product_pack_error_status(...)==503 (MCP), never unconditionally -- a blanket retry hint on the 400 branch would have been a NEW defect (telling a caller to retry a permanent validation failure)
summary: get_definition/export_definition (both sides) and list_product_packs/get_product_pack (both sides, conditionally on the 503 classification only) now carry correct retry hints

trigger: preflight_routes.cpp's GET /api/v1/preflight/runs and deployment_routes.cpp's GET /api/v1/deployments/preview both omit retry_after_ms on their unavailable/degraded branches, while their OWN MCP twins (list_preflight_runs/get_deployment_preview) already correctly pass retry_after_ms=kMcpStoreFaultShortRetryMs (2000) on the identical branches -- this is the INVERSE direction from the Guardian/Workflows findings: REST was the side missing it, not MCP, corroborating what #4226's own colleague review said (and correcting #4242's review, which mislabeled it the same class as Guardian's gap)
provenance: read mcp_retry.hpp directly to confirm kMcpStoreFaultShortRetryMs=2000 (distinct from kMcpStoreFaultRetryMs=5000, a deliberate domain-specific pricing per that header's own comment); applied retry_after_ms=2000 (not 5000) to REST's 4 branches (2 in preflight_routes.cpp, 2 in deployment_routes.cpp) to match the MCP twin's own already-chosen value, not REST's more common 5000 literal used elsewhere
summary: 4 REST branches (2 preflight_routes.cpp, 2 deployment_routes.cpp) now carry retry_after_ms=2000, matching their own MCP twins exactly
caused_by: #4036 original implementation (REST side under-specified vs its own MCP twin)

trigger: list_guardian_events' MCP input schema left rule_id and severity as bare {"type":"string"} with no maxLength, flagged on #4242's colleague review as missing the repo's new-tool schema floor -- REST's own OpenAPI schema for the same route also has no maxLength on these two params, confirming this predates and is not unique to the MCP twin
provenance: checked REST's OpenAPI parameter definitions for rule_id/severity directly (rest_api_v1.cpp) -- both unbounded there too; chose maxLength:256 to match the existing agent_id field's own bound in the same schema literal, the only established precedent in this exact tool's schema
summary: list_guardian_events' rule_id and severity input fields now carry maxLength:256, matching agent_id's existing bound in the same schema

trigger: the first design attempt for scripts/ci/check-mcp-retry-hints.py scanned the WHOLE file unconditionally (structural call-assigned-guard heuristic, no diff scoping) and produced 103 flagged sites, the overwhelming majority of which were verified-by-hand to be false positives (existence checks, business-rule 409s, input-parse failures -- e.g. `existing`, `revoked`, `tokens`, `limit_opt`, `overlap_days_opt`) rather than genuine store/query-fault conditions -- a repo-wide lexical retrofit of this class of check is not tractable without an unmaintainable hand-curated allowlist covering the majority of ~100+ pre-existing call sites
provenance: redesigned as a diff-aware check scoped to NEW kTools[] entries only, matching A5's own wording ('every new/materially-changed MCP tool'); validated against real history in both directions: run against the actual #4037 merge (78e008547..2767e44a8) it correctly flags 4 of the 5 known-real gaps (missing get_guardian_device_guards, whose guard variable assignment is separated from its if(!x) check by an intervening audit-call statement -- a known, documented lexical-tripwire limitation, not silently unaddressed); run against the actual #4034 merge (already-correct implementation) it correctly reports 0 gaps on 3 new tools, zero false positives
summary: The retry-hint CI gate is scoped to new/changed tools only (matching A5's own wording), not a repo-wide retrofit; validated against real historical PR merges in both directions (catches known-real gaps, no false positives on known-clean code) before being wired into CI

trigger: proportionate regression-test coverage decision: writing a full PG-fault-injection or corruption-hook integration test for all 13 fixed call sites individually would be materially more expensive than the fix itself; a lightweight unreachable-PgPool mechanism (matching the existing 'MCP list_executions: a degraded tracker...' test precedent) works for GuaranteedStateStore (its guard is a bare pointer-null check, so a never-opened-but-non-null store still reaches the query-fault branch) but NOT for WorkflowEngine/ProductPackStore (both gate on is_open(), which correctly returns false on an unreachable pool at construction, so the lightweight trick trips the WRONG -- correctly-non-retryable -- branch instead)
provenance: wrote and ran a WorkflowEngine version of the same test first; it failed at the is_open() REQUIRE (false, not true as assumed from a stale header comment describing historical behavior) -- read the actual constructor (workflow_engine.cpp:363-378) to confirm is_open() is gated on a real pool.acquire() + migration check, not unconditional; removed the test rather than build the heavier live-PG-corruption-hook fixture for one additional regression proof, given the fix itself is a mechanically-verified, low-risk, identically-shaped change across all 13 sites and the new CI gate independently validates the SAME bug class going forward for any future tool
summary: One regression test written and passing (get_guardian_status, using the lightweight unreachable-pool mechanism); the analogous Workflows test was attempted, found infeasible with the lightweight mechanism, and removed rather than left broken or built with a heavier fixture -- remaining 12 sites covered by manual code-read verification + the new CI gate's forward-looking enforcement, not by dedicated regression tests
waiver_rationale: proportionate testing given the fix's low-risk, mechanically-uniform shape and the new CI gate's independent forward-looking coverage of the same defect class
